title: Calzone Ricotta e Salame
subtitle: Baked pizza pocket with ricotta and cured ham
excerpt: Calzone is a pizza disc folded in half over a filling of ricotta, mozzarella, and cured ham, then baked in a very hot oven. The sealed edge puffs and the filling steams inside the crust. It is served with tomato sauce on top, not inside.
sourceNotes: Calzone is a Neapolitan baked pasta pizza pocket, documented in the Naples region since at least the 18th century. The name means 'trouser leg' or 'stocking' in Neapolitan dialect, referring to the folded shape. The traditional filling is ricotta and salami or prosciutto; the tomato sauce served alongside or on top is a modern addition.

recipe.makeAheadNotes: Prepare the dough 24 hours ahead. Mix the filling up to 2 hours before baking.
recipe.temperatureNote: Fan or conventional, maximum oven setting. Preheat with a pizza stone or heavy tray for at least 45 minutes.

content.text: A calzone is a pizza disc folded over a filling of ricotta, mozzarella, and prosciutto. The sealed edge puffs up in the oven and the filling cooks inside with no contact with the oven air, so it stays creamy and moist. Tomato sauce goes on top after baking, not inside, because it would make the base soft and prevent the crust from crisping.
You need one 210 g ball of 24-hour pizza dough per calzone, rested at room temperature for 2 hours before shaping.
Heat the oven to maximum with a heavy tray or pizza stone on the top shelf. Preheat for 45 minutes.
Mix the ricotta, mozzarella, prosciutto, parmesan, black pepper, and salt together in a bowl.
Stretch one dough ball into a rough 30 cm disc. Spoon a quarter of the filling onto one half of the disc, leaving a 2 cm border at the edge.
Fold the unfilled half over the filling to form a half-moon. Press and crimp the edges firmly all the way around to seal. Brush the top with olive oil.
Slide the calzone onto the hot tray. Bake for 12 to 15 minutes until deep golden and puffed. The sealed edge should be firm and not leaking.
Spoon the warmed passata over the top of the calzone or serve it in a small bowl alongside. Eat immediately.

Calzone is Neapolitan, from the same tradition as pizza Margherita. The name translates roughly as 'trouser leg', a reference to the shape. In Naples it is a pizzeria staple; the filling varies by cook, but ricotta and salumi are the most traditional combination. The version with tomato inside the pocket, common in some countries, is considered inauthentic in Naples.
